newsitem.title: UK: UK retail shares inch up on Christmas sales hopes.
newsitem.headline: UK retail shares inch up on Christmas sales hopes.

text.p: Shares in UK retailers were generally higher on Monday as investors hoped British stores would report bumper sales over the Christmas period, dealers said.

"It is looking like the retail sector had a pretty good Christmas," one market maker said. "Retail stocks are on a lot of fund managers lists for 1997 so we're seeing a bit of interest in the sector today."
Trading volume was light, however, as many players remained absent ahead of the New Year holidays, he said. The London share market is open for only a half day on Tuesday.
UK financial markets are shut on Wednesday, January 1 but return to normal trading hours on Thursday, January 2.
Amongst leading retailers, Marks & Spencer was up 3-1/2p at 485p, Argos rose 4-1/2p to 774-1/2p, Kingfisher gained 4p to 624-1/2p, and Dixons added 1p to 530-1/2p.
